page: Amazon Web Services m8idb.metal-96xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C x86_64 processors. The instance delivers 192 physical cores and 384 dedicated vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of L3 cache. System memory comprises 1536 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, preserving a balanced general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions for targeted matrix and vector compute operations.

Storage and networking subsystems are configured for high-throughput environments. The server bundles 22800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, providing massive non-volatile disk capacity directly on the physical host. Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 400 Gbps. The server operates without discrete GPU accelerators, dedicating all onboard resources to x86 compute, memory, and high-bandwidth interconnect operations.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional parallel execution and memory bandwidth. The system achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing (412041.97) and Redis SET operations (476.52 million operations per second), alongside 1170.68 GB/sec in uncached large-block read operations. Static web serving throughput measures at 160.32 GB/sec. In contrast, single-threaded metrics sit within the middle tier, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1944.6, and sequential LLM token generation remaining modest.

The dense core count, 1.5 TB memory allocation, and large local NVMe storage deliver strong resource consolidation efficiency for distributed systems. The instance is suited for high-throughput transactional and analytical databases, large-scale Redis in-memory caching clusters, static web serving infrastructure, enterprise ETL workflows, and container host environments requiring significant parallel execution and fast local scratch space.
